articles.title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Darian Mensah, Trinidad Chambliss Join Dante Moore, Arch Manning in Round 1
articles.summary: The college football season is entering Week 2 and the NFL season is just getting started, which means 2027 NFL mock drafts are also in full effect. Early in...
articles.body:
The college football season is entering Week 2 and the NFL season is just getting started, which means 2027 NFL mock drafts are also in full effect.

Early in the college football season, several players have put their names on the NFL Draft radar, and they have the rest of 2026 to prove why they should be selected on Day 1.

Now, in Week 1 of the NFL season, let's use PFN's Mock Draft Simulator to project how the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft currently stacks up.

In my last mock draft , we had some fun as the New York Jets acquired the No. 1 overall pick in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. However, in this go-around, we'll get straight to business, leading the Cardinals to draft a new franchise quarterback in Dante Moore.

Arizona recently extended Michael Wilson , and Marvin Harrison Jr. will be looking for an extension of his own next offseason. It's crucial for Arizona to find its gunslinger of the future.

As for Moore, he is the No. 1-ranked quarterback on PFN's 2027 NFL Draft Big Board . With this season of development, there is a legitimate chance the Oregon product will be ready to start on Sundays as a rookie.

A no-brainer decision for the Miami Dolphins, bringing home Jeremiah Smith not only gives them the best receiver in the draft but also gives the fans a reason to show up and show out in the midst of a rebuild.

Considered a perennial top-five selection since his first snap at Ohio State, Smith already began the year with an electric performance, as he put up 151 yards and 2 touchdowns in the first half against Ball State. Smith is picking up right where he left off and proving to scouts that he's still the best receiver in college football.

As of now, Arch Manning is still the only other quarterback who could claim the QB1 slot in the 2027 NFL Draft. Still, with Dante Moore going No. 1 overall, this gives the New York Jets a chance to build around the 6-foot-4, mobile Manning, with several talented pieces already around their quarterback of the future.

It's clear that Geno Smith is nothing more than a bridge quarterback for the 2026 season, so the Jets will likely be all-in on finding a face of the franchise after this year. Manning is expected to lead Texas through a competitive SEC, so perhaps a CFP run and Heisman trophy push would make him a lock to be one of the top two quarterbacks in 2027.

There just doesn't seem to be a light at either end of the tunnel when it comes to the Cleveland Browns' quarterback options this season. Whether it's Shedeur Sanders , Deshaun Watson , or even Dillon Gabriel , none of these quarterbacks should be starting for Cleveland in 2027.

This takes us to Miami's Darian Mensah, another rising talent in next year's draft class who not only has a strong resume but also the skill set to back it up. He started his 2026 campaign with a 400-yard, 5-touchdown outing, putting him in early Heisman conversations.

A run at the Heisman trophy and a CFP push for the Hurricanes just may be the bump Mensah needs to become a legitimate first-round candidate.

This is almost a no-brainer selection when you look at the Las Vegas Raiders' depth chart, as drafting Texas WR Cam Coleman will instantly provide the offense with a legitimate WR1 candidate and also help relieve some pressure from the team's leading pass catcher, tight end Brock Bowers .

After selecting Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft, giving him a legitimate weapon on the outside has to be priority No. 1 for Las Vegas. Given that the franchise has already heavily invested in the offense over the past few years, a new wide receiver in the first round could be on schedule for the Raiders.

The Atlanta Falcons are a tricky team to project in mock drafts due to the lingering questions surrounding the quarterback position. After investing the No. 8 overall pick in Michael Penix Jr. in 2024, perhaps Atlanta holds off on taking another early-round arm and instead reinforces its offensive line to not only keep Penix upright, but also keep Bijan Robinson happy, too.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Jake Matthews has been a steady presence for over a decade, but he's in the later stages of his career, and the Falcons need a young tackle ready to take the baton. Jordan Seaton was starting in a Power Four conference from the moment he stepped on campus, and he's only gotten more polished since.

Taking Seaton here gives Atlanta a cornerstone blocker who can protect its young passer, open lanes for its star back, and keep the offense on track for the next decade.

The Tennessee Titans spent the last few drafts rebuilding their offense, and now it's time to give the defense a real closer off the edge. With Jermaine Johnson II heading into the final year of his rookie deal, the Titans can't afford to wait on finding their next long-term pass rusher if an extension isn't on the horizon.

Colin Simmons brings the kind of first-step burst that makes tackles panic before the snap, and he's already making his presence felt this fall with a fumble recovery in the opener. He's the type of player who changes games in the fourth quarter, and pairing him with Jeffery Simmons up front would give Tennessee a disruptive duo to build the defense around.

The Carolina Panthers have their lockdown corner on one side with Jaycee Horn , but the spot opposite him is still a question mark. Leonard Moore has been battle-tested since he was a freshman and is now regarded as the best cornerback in the class.

His length and patience in press coverage make him a natural fit for a secondary that wants to play aggressive man coverage, and he allows the Panthers to form a young corner tandem that could hold up against anyone in the division.

The New Orleans Saints' pass rush has leaned on veterans for years, and that window is closing. Quincy Rhodes Jr. out of Arkansas offers a massive frame with long arms that let him win the leverage battle before blockers can get their hands on him.

He's still ascending, which is exactly what a rebuilding defense should want at this spot. New Orleans gets a high-ceiling rusher who can set the edge against the run on Day 1 while his pass-rush game keeps developing.

The New York Giants have always believed games are won in the trenches, and David Stone fits that identity perfectly. He's a former blue-chip recruit with rare power for his size and he's capable of collapsing the pocket from the interior, where quarterbacks feel the most pressure.

Adding him to a defensive front that already has talent on the edges would make it nearly impossible for offenses to slide protection to one side without paying for it elsewhere.

The Washington Commanders need more youth and range on the back end, and Tae Johnson brings a smart, instinctive presence to the secondary.

Notre Dame's defense asks its safeties to handle a lot mentally, and he's comfortable rotating late, disguising coverages, and coming downhill to make tackles in space.

He'd give the Commanders a versatile chess piece who can play deep, drop into the box, or match up with tight ends in an NFC East loaded with weapons.

After moving on from Sauce Gardner , the Jets continue to have a hole at the premium position in their secondary, and Ellis Robinson IV is the perfect candidate to fill it.

Georgia's defense produces pro-ready corners year after year, and he's cut from that same cloth with fluid hips, sticky coverage, and the confidence to challenge receivers at the catch point. New York rebuilds its cornerback room with a player who can grow into a true CB1.

As the backfield ages, the offense needs a young runner to carry the load for the Minnesota Vikings. Miami's Jadan Baugh runs with a downhill style that wears defenses down as the game goes on, but he also has enough burst to turn a simple inside run into a chunk play.

In an offense that thrives on play-action, having a back that defenses actually fear makes everything else easier, especially for a young quarterback still finding his footing.

The Pittsburgh Steelers have been searching for their long-term answer at quarterback since Ben Roethlisberger retired, and Trinidad Chambliss might be the most intriguing option in this class. His journey from Division II to leading an SEC offense shows toughness and a chip on his shoulder that fits the Steelers' culture.

He extends plays with his legs, throws with confidence off-platform, and has a knack for rising in big moments. Pittsburgh finally takes its swing at the position instead of patching it with veterans.

With their second pick in the first round, the Jets give their offense another weapon. Garrett Wilson needs a running mate who can take attention away from him and let rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. thrive as well.

The Jets decide to dip back into the Indiana factory once again, selecting Charlie Becker, who has shown he can stretch the field and win in contested situations. His ability to create explosive plays makes him an ideal complement, giving whoever is under center in New York a much bigger margin for error.

The Chicago Bears' defense still needs another pass rusher to go with Montez Sweat . Dylan Stewart is one of the most explosive edge players in the country, with the twitch and bend to flatten around the corner in a flash.

Stewart plays with a relentless motor that shows up on every down for his team. He did fall in this week's mock draft simply because he missed Week 1 with a back injury, which may also keep him out of Week 2's contest, raising some concern about his medicals.

The Cincinnati Bengals have invested heavily in keeping franchise quarterback Joe Burrow upright, but both starting guards are on a limited time, and the line needs a long-term piece in the middle.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Austin Siereveld fits that need perfectly. He's a physical, heavy-handed blocker with experience lining up at multiple spots, giving the Bengals flexibility if injuries hit.

The Jacksonville Jaguars have talent coming off the edges, but the interior needs someone who can command double teams and free up those rushers. Scott is a thick, powerful tackle who plays with surprising quickness off the snap, and he has a habit of living in the backfield before guards can get set.

Putting him in the middle of the Jaguars' front gives their edge players more one-on-one chances and makes the defense far tougher to run on.

Mississippi State's Kelley Jones brings a long, rangy frame that lets him disrupt receivers at the line, a profile that has become the prototype in today's NFL. Tampa Bay's defense requires corners who can hold up on an island, and Jones can do just that.

He's a natural competitor at the catch point, and he gives the Bucs a young cornerback who can match up with the big-bodied receivers they face in the NFC South.

Denver's defense has become one of the most feared units in the league, thanks in part to its pass rush, and the smart move is keeping that pipeline full. Yhonzae Pierre is a rusher who wins with speed and a nonstop motor, the kind of player who offensive coordinators have to account for on every snap.

Adding him to an already deep rotation would keep the Broncos' pressure relentless for all four quarters and set them up for the future as contracts come due.

The Houston Texans have built a young, confident defense, and KJ Bolden would slide right into that identity. Coming out of Georgia's system, he's used to handling a heavy mental load, and he has the range to cover ground from the deep middle while still showing up as a physical tackler near the line of scrimmage.

He's a former top recruit who plays like it, and he gives the Texans a secondary with the speed and versatility to keep up with any offense in the league.

With Lane Johnson in the later stages of his career, Texas offensive lineman Trevor Goosby is the perfect succession plan. He's a long, athletic tackle with the footwork to mirror speed rushers and the frame to keep adding strength.

The Philadelphia Eagles can develop him behind their veterans and hand him the keys when the time comes, keeping one of the NFL's best lines rolling and one of the top backfields protected.

Detroit's aggressive defensive style puts a lot of pressure on its cornerbacks, and adding another young, competitive corner makes sense, especially given Terrion Arnold 's departure in the offseason.

Ashton Hampton fits the Lions' gritty mentality and gives them a secondary that can hold up against the high-powered passing attacks they'll see deep into January.

Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh wants a defense that plays fast and physical, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa checks both boxes.

He's an instinctive linebacker who flies sideline to sideline, fills running lanes with bad intentions, and has the athleticism to hang with backs and tight ends in coverage. He'd give Los Angeles a three-down linebacker who can be the heartbeat of the defense for years to come.

Protecting Drake Maye is New England 's top priority, and Carter Smith keeps that mission going. He's a steady, technically sound tackle who helped anchor one of the most impressive offenses in college football.

Smith plays with patience and balance in pass protection and has the toughness to finish blocks in the run game. Pairing him with the Patriots' existing young linemen gives them a foundation up front that could last a long time.

The San Francisco 49ers and Kyle Shanahan's offense depend on its line executing a zone-heavy run scheme with precision, and Minnesota's Greg Johnson has the mobility and awareness to thrive in it.

He gets to the second level quickly, seals off linebackers, and keeps his feet moving through contact. With the 49ers needing to get younger and cheaper on the interior, Johnson is a plug-and-play option who fits the system from Day 1.

If George Pickens walks in free agency, Dallas can't leave CeeDee Lamb without a legit running mate. ASU's Omarion Miller is a dynamic playmaker who can line up outside and take the top off a defense, but he's also dangerous after the catch on quick throws.

The Sun Devil would give the Cowboys a young, explosive target to keep defenses from rolling coverage toward Lamb and ensure the passing game doesn't miss a beat.

Kansas City 's championship formula starts with keeping Patrick Mahomes comfortable, and the tackle spots have been a recurring concern. Melvin Siani is a physical blocker with the size to handle bull rushers and the grit to hold up in big moments.

Adding him gives the Chiefs a young bookend who can grow into a starter and give their star quarterback the time he needs to create magic.

Baltimore always values smart, physical defensive backs, and Miami's OJ Frederique Jr. is just the player this describes. He earned playing time early in his college career and has only gotten better, showing strong instincts, quick recovery speed, and a willingness to come up and tackle.

Giving the Ravens another young corner to go alongside their talented secondary helps them stay ahead in a division full of explosive receivers.

A'Mauri Washington is a massive, powerful interior lineman who eats up blockers and makes it hard for offenses to run between the tackles.

His ability to push the pocket from the inside creates chances for everyone else on the front, and he gives the Seahawks a cornerstone in the middle of their defense for years to come.

DJ Moore was a great addition to provide Josh Allen a legit WR1 on the outside, but other than Khalil Shakir , the Bills really don't have much firepower at the receiver position. Granted, Skyler Bell is still set to kick off his rookie season as the WR3/4 for Buffalo, so that remains to be seen.

Still, the Bills should be all in on finding a young, dynamic weapon for their offense, given that the Keon Coleman experiment has failed. Indiana's Nick Marsh would give the receiving room a significant boost and a legitimate trio of playmakers at wideout.

With Myles Garrett gone, Cleveland has a massive void to fill on the edge, and there's no replacing a player like that with a stopgap. The Browns need a young rusher who can solidify the defensive front alongside Jared Verse and Mason Graham . Oregon's Matayo Uiagalelei has the tools to grow into that role.

Uiagalelei may not be asked to carry the pass rush on Day 1, but he has the size, motor, and upside to become the new tone-setter for a defense searching for its next identity.

articles.title: How Arizona Cardinals can make 2026 season a success
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals may not be heading for the playoffs in 2026. But that doesn't mean this season can't be a success. Here's the blueprint.
articles.body:
If there's one thing Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur has made clear since arriving in Arizona , it's this: He knows the challenge ahead.

It would be difficult not to. LaFleur spent the majority of his NFL career working for Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay, with a daily view of their brilliance as offensive minds. And he spent the past two seasons preparing game plans to face Mike Macdonald, the defensive wizard who forged the Seahawks into a Super Bowl champion.

Compared to those rivals, the Cardinals have spent recent seasons operating in a different orbit. So when asked last week about the NFL's constantly expanding schedule, LaFleur acknowledged as much.

"We play 17 Sundays in the daytime, and I think we all understand why," LaFleur said. "If we want to play in those primetime slots and on Wednesdays and Thursdays and Netflix and all those things, we've gotta go earn those spots."

Arizona Cardinals uniforms through the years

That begs a follow-up question: What would it take for the Cardinals to "earn those spots?" In other words, what does a successful season look like in Arizona?

In this division — with this roster and this schedule — asking for a playoff push is asking for disappointment. But that doesn't mean there's nothing to play for — far from it.

One answer is obvious: If Carson Beck emerges as the franchise quarterback, little else matters. The history of third-round quarterbacks, though, tells us that's a long shot. So for the sake of this exercise, let's focus elsewhere.

The other simple answer would be landing the No. 1 pick. Certainly, if either Arch Manning or Dante Moore establishes himself as a generational prospect, that would be appealing.

But it's also a risky path. Excluding Fernando Mendoza — since he hasn't yet played an NFL snap — seven quarterbacks have been drafted No. 1 overall in the past decade. Only one of those players, Joe Burrow , has successfully and lastingly transformed a franchise. The median outcome from those selections is arguably Kyler Murray , living proof that the No. 1 pick is not a silver bullet, at least not without sufficient supporting infrastructure.

For the Cardinals, though, there's another path that may be both more sustainable and more attainable.

Imagine a world where, come January, the Cardinals look to be a quarterback away from contention. It might not be as far-fetched as it sounds.

By the end of the season, Mike LaFleur could look like the next standout playcaller to have served as McVay's offensive coordinator.

History is on his side, given that the previous three were Matt LaFleur, Kevin O'Connell and Liam Coen. So too was the Cardinals' preseason performance, when their offense led the NFL in yards per game. LaFleur poured cold water on that, saying he puts "zero" stock in preseason numbers, but his players disagree.

"I think a lot of that is coaching," Michael Wilson said. "… It's getting the right calls in, the way that Mike and the offensive staff are detailing things up in the pass game, getting guys open, getting guys advantageous 1-on-1s."

And if LaFleur's playcalling success can translate to the regular season, could the Cardinals prove to have a top-10 offensive infrastructure surrounding their quarterback? Again, it's more realistic than it may seem.

After Jacoby Brissett took over as the starter last season, there were four games in which Marvin Harrison Jr. played more than 60% of offensive snaps. In those games, the Cardinals ranked 15th in expected points added per dropback, despite virtually no rushing threat. With their top two running backs sidelined, they ranked 26th in EPA per carry in those same games.

Now, a prodigiously talented Jeremiyah Love enters the mix, along with a reliable veteran in Tyler Allgeier . That's a significant upgrade on the three-headed committee of Bam Knight , Michael Carter and Emari Demercado .

Plus, the offensive line should be improved. In those same weeks, the most common configuration up front was Paris Johnson Jr. , Evan Brown , Hjalte Froholdt , Will Hernandez and Jonah Williams . Using PFF grades as a proxy, each of the Cardinals' three new starters is an upgrade.

And it's the second year under offensive line coach Justin Frye for that group, at the position where coaching matters most.

"He's found his way of doing it," Froholdt said. "And I think we've all bought into it."

Put it all together, and the Cardinals can reasonably aim to be a top half offense. And that's with Brissett, who may be a reliable distributor but is far from a true franchise quarterback. If the Cardinals finish, say, 15th in total offense this season, it would be easy to envision something grander in 2027, with a new quarterback in town.

The picture is no doubt murkier for the defense.

The state of the roster is especially troubling up front, where only one current player recorded more than two sacks last season. If the Cardinals finish bottom five in both pressure rate and yards per carry allowed, it won't come as a surprise. And at linebacker and safety, they are set to start a pair of players who commanded a combined $6.7 million in free agency — players whom the league has revealed it doesn't value. Whereas the offense may be top 15, the defense clearly projects as bottom 10.

But a few factors could still stoke optimism.

The first, naturally, is health, after the 2025 Cardinals set unwanted records in that department. That situation fully unraveled in Week 9, when linebacker Mack Wilson Sr. and cornerback Will Johnson both went down. Wilson missed the rest of the season, while Johnson turned into a shell of himself. Before the injury, he had an 85.7 passer rating when targeted. After the injury, that number was 139.4.

The impact of those injuries was clear. In Weeks 1-9, the Cardinals ranked 10th in Defense-adjusted Value Over Average (DVOA), which accounts for strength of opponent. In Weeks 10-18, they ranked 28th.

Finishing anywhere near 10th is likely unrealistic, given that the Cardinals lost Calais Campbell and Jalen Thompson without acquiring clear replacements. Still, they should avoid being as woeful as they were down the stretch.

Plus, defense is volatile. Among the 10 worst defenses (based on DVOA) in 2024, three became top-10 units last season. A poor 2026 on that side of the ball wouldn't spell doom for 2027 and beyond.

And with Josh Sweat , Walter Nolen , Will Johnson and Budda Baker , the Cardinals may end the year with two high-level players in both the front and the secondary. That's a useful foundation, even if that quartet is currently surrounded by worrisome cracks. Add in some development for young players like Jordan Burch , Cody Simon and Max Melton , and the list of needs may be short enough to address in one offseason.

Play this scenario out: The Cardinals enter the offseason in need of a defensive tackle, an edge rusher and a safety. With $108 million in projected effective cap space, per Over The Cap, that's a realistic shopping list, even if Michael Wilson commands a healthy extension.

What could this mean for the future Cardinals?

So let's put the pieces together here. The Cardinals could have a promising new play-calling head coach, with a top-10 offensive infrastructure and defensive building blocks at the most important positions. And because of their current flaws, those strengths could still be paired with abundant cap space and a top-five pick in what's expected to be a strong quarterback class.

Instead of drafting a quarterback first overall with no supporting cast, this could be a case of drafting a top-10 quarterback into a situation built for a quick turnaround.

That certainly wouldn't erase every question surrounding the Cardinals. If they finish, say, 5-12, general manager Monti Ossenfort would be entering the offseason with a 20-48 record at the helm. That's uneven footing for a decision-maker tasked with drafting a new franchise quarterback.

But it's not a bad outlook. And it may be more attainable than it seems today, on the eve of a season that arrives with historically low expectations.

articles.title: Robert Saleh's Revenge Game vs. Jets Discussed by Insiders, Titans HC Will 'Be After Their Asses'
articles.summary: Robert Saleh's first game as head coach of the Tennessee Titans will take on a special meaning for him because it also comes against the New York Jets team that unceremoniously fired him midway through the 2024 season.
articles.body:
Robert Saleh's first game as head coach of the Tennessee Titans will take on a special meaning for him because it also comes against the New York Jets team that unceremoniously fired him midway through the 2024 season.

Speaking to ESPN's Turron Davenport and Rich Cimini , one former Jets player explained how they think Saleh is approaching Sunday's matchup.

"Saleh will be after their asses," the player said.

The Jets gave Saleh his first opportunity as a head coach in the NFL. He went 20-36 with no playoff appearances in four seasons before being fired after a Week 5 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in October 2024.

Even though the Jets never took the step forward during Saleh's tenure they were hoping for, their seven wins in both 2022 and 2023 are tied for their most in a single-season since 2016.

Davenport and Cimini noted Saleh and Jets owner Woody Johnson didn't have a "close rapport" during that period, in part because Johnson wasn't the one who hired him since he was serving out his tenure as the U.S. ambassador to the United Kingdom when Saleh got the job in January 2021.

According to Davenport and Cimini, Johnson's public message in the wake of Saleh's firing was "I just think we can do better."

The Jets are 6-23 since moving on from Saleh. Their 14 losses in 2025 tied the second-most in a single season in franchise history.

Saleh spent last season as defensive coordinator for the San Francisco 49ers. He was hired by the Titans as their new head coach in January.

Sunday will mark Saleh's first game against the Jets as either a head coach or coordinator since he was fired. It will kickoff on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET from Nissan Stadium.

articles.body:
The NFL played two of its 16 Week 1 matchups, Wednesday's New England Patriots-Seattle Seahawks opener and Thursday's San Francisco 49ers-Los Angeles Rams game in Melbourne, and now waits until Sunday for the rest of the slate.

College football fills that gap tonight, and it's doing it with the No. 1 team in the country walking into Austin. Ohio State takes on Texas at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC, a rematch of last year's opener that the Buckeyes won 14-7, except this time, both programs enter ranked in the top four.

Catch College Football Action On Saturday: Schedule & Streaming Details

The marquee matchup arrives at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC, when No. 1 Ohio State visits No. 4 Texas in Austin. In that same primetime window, Louisiana Tech visits No. 8 LSU on SECN+, and No. 13 Texas Tech travels to Oregon State on CBS.

The day opens with a stacked noon slate with No. 6 Oregon at Oklahoma State on ESPN, Howard at No. 5 Indiana on Big Ten Network, Arizona State at No. 10 Texas A&M on ABC, No. 11 Oklahoma at Michigan on FOX, and No. 16 Penn State at Temple on ESPN2.

That Indiana game is worth watching for a different reason, with the Hoosiers entering as the reigning national champions.

Having beaten Miami in the title game to close last season, they face their first real test of the new campaign against an FCS opponent on Saturday.

Western Kentucky visits No. 2 Georgia at 12:45 p.m. ET on SEC Network.

The afternoon window sends Rice to No. 3 Notre Dame at 3:30 p.m. ET on NBC. Notre Dame missed the College Football Playoff last season despite finishing 10-2 and enters this year still ranked among the nation's elite under its current staff.

The rest of the afternoon slate includes No. 12 Alabama at Kentucky on ABC, Arizona at No. 15 BYU on FOX, and Utah State at No. 19 Washington on Big Ten Network. UC Davis visits No. 17 SMU at 4 p.m. ET on ACCNX.

The evening card before primetime features No. 18 Tennessee at Georgia Tech at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN and Southern at No. 22 Houston on ESPN+.

articles.title: Every NFL Teams' Most Important 2027 Free Agent Entering Week 1
articles.summary: We're now two games into the 2026 NFL season, which means the march to Super Bowl LXI has officially begun. For the coaches and players hoping to chase a championship, the focus is firmly on the here and now.
articles.body:
We're now two games into the 2026 NFL season, which means the march to Super Bowl LXI has officially begun. For the coaches and players hoping to chase a championship, the focus is firmly on the here and now.

However, team decision-makers already have one eye on the future and the 2027 offseason. This is why we saw a flurry of extensions—involving players like Baker Mayfield, Michael Wilson, and Jameis Winston—just before the start of Week 1.

Franchises rarely want to part with valuable long-term contributors, and we're sure to see several notable 2027 free agenct receive new contracts between now and the spring. Who are the likeliest candidates? That's what we're here to examine.

We'll examine each team's most important impending 2027 free agent based on factors like past production, player upside, projected role, and positional value. The caveat is that this is an early look at next year's free-agent class, and the players who are most important to each franchise could easily change in the coming months.

This is one of those aforementioned situations that could change significantly over the course of the 2026 season.

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett started 12 games for the Arizona Cardinals in 2025 and posted a respectable 94.1 passer rating. He's entering Week 1 as the starter, and while he'll turn 34 in December, he would be a valuable bridge candidate if the Cardinals draft a quarterback early in 2027.

However, there's a non-zero chance that Arizona will pivot to third-round rookie Carson Beck at some point this season. If that happens, and the Cardinals are pleased with Beck's development, Arizona may search for a more budget-friendly understudy to fill the QB2 role.

Plus, Brissett may want the opportunity to start elsewhere, even in a bridge role.

Safety Jessie Bates III will turn 30 in February, but he remains one of the most important pieces in the Atlanta Falcons defense. A second-team All-Pro in 2025, Bates started all 17 games and played a whopping 99 percent of the defensive snaps.

Bates finished this past season with 98 tackles, six passes defended, three interceptions, one forced fumble, and one tackle for loss. He was arguably the key cog on the back end of Jeff Ulbrich's defense.

Retaining Bates should be a priority for the Falcons, as it appears that Ulbrich will oversee the defense for the foreseeable future. He was hired as the defensive coordinator last offseason, and he was given a three-year extension shortly after Kevin Stefanski was hired as the new head coach in January.

Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey will turn 31 next offseason and saw a dip in his level of play this past season. However, the Ravens are confident that he'll bounce back in 2026.

"[He] did not have a great year last year," general manager Eric DeCosta told reporters in early September. "I feel confident he is going to rebound and have a great year this year."

Humphrey's not-great year included 15 starts, four interceptions, and an opposing passer rating of 84.6 . Those would be considered strong numbers for a lot of other cornerbacks around the league.

Of course, Humphrey was a first-team All-Pro two years ago. If he can come close to matching his 2024 performance, DeCosta should be eager to keep Humphrey in the fold on another contract.

The Buffalo Bills don't have an extensive list of impending 2027 free agents, as the franchise has a tendency to lock up key players early. However, Dorian Williams is one important contributor who could potentially get away in the spring.

A 2023 third-round pick out of Tulane, Williams hasn't been a full-time starter, but he's been a valuable role player, especially in three-linebacker formations. He appeared in 16 games last season and recorded 63 tackles and a fumble recovery while playing 47 percent of the defensive snaps.

In all, Williams has appeared in 50 games with 22 starts and has recorded 220 combined tackles. He'll only turn 26 next summer.

Mike Jackson might not be a household name, but the Carolina Panthers cornerback could be one of the best bargain free agents available in 2027 if he hits the open market.

While Jackson will turn 30 in January, he was a high-level starter for the Panthers in 2025. He appeared in all 17 games and played 99 percent of the defensive snaps. He logged four interceptions and a league-high 19 passes defended (tied), while allowing an opposing passer rating of only 75.0 in coverage.

Jaycee Horn might be the star of Carolina's secondary, but Jackson is the perfect complement to him in Ejiro Evero's defense. If he can replicate his 2025 performance, it'll be difficult to justify letting him walk.

Running back D'Andre Swift was a candidate here, as he's led the Chicago Bears' backfield rotation for the past two seasons. However, he signed a three-year extension on Friday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson now becomes a clearer choice.

Stevenson has largely served as Chicago's No. 2 perimeter corner opposite standout Jaylon Johnson. He was limited to 13 games by a hip injury last season, but he made 10 starts and allowed an opposing passer rating of just 86.3 in coverage.

While Stevenson may be challenged by rookie Malik Muhammad at some point this season, the fourth-round pick out of Texas is likely to push for time in the slot initially. Stevenson is only 26 years old, and if he can stay healthy and hold down the perimeter job, he should earn a second contract in Chicago.

The Cincinnati Bengals finally decided to invest in their defense this offseason. Assuming their focus on defense wasn't a one-off occurrence, cornerbacks D.J. Turner II and Dax Hill should both be priorities in the 2027 offseason.

Running back Chase Brown is also set to be a free agent in the spring, though he should be easier to replace, given the rest of the offensive supporting cast.

Turner was the more efficient of the two defensive backs in 2025 and appears to be on the verge of establishing himself as a top-10 cover man. The 26-year-old appeared in all 17 games last season, recorded two interceptions, and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 75.6 in coverage.

Defensive tackle Maliek Collins has his 2025 campaign ended prematurely by a torn quad. However, while he opened training camp on the physically unable to perform list, he was activated in late August and could be ready for early-season action.

If Collins is healthy and can approach last season's form, he should be a top priority for the rebuilding Cleveland Browns. Quality defensive tackles are tough to find, and Collins has shown that he can be a disruptive force in Cleveland.

Collins started all 12 games in which he appeared last season, and he amassed 25 tackles, 6.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, and 15 QB pressures. He'll turn 32 in April, but he can be a centerpiece of the Browns' defensive-line rotation, alongside 2025 first-round pick Mason Graham.

Dallas Cowboys receiver George Pickens made our preseason top-10 list of 2027 free agents for a reason. Though he'll need to prove that he can replicate last year's success, Pickens' first campaign in Dallas proved that he can be an elite offensive playmaker.

Pickens caught 93 passes for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns last season. Pairing him with CeeDee Lamb was the catalyst behind an offense that might just be Super Bowl caliber in 2026. While the Cowboys were forced to keep Pickens via the franchise tag, franchise owner Jerry Jones sounds quite open to keeping him long-term.

"I'm excited what he has to do with us this year and in coming years, and I emphasize that, in coming years," Jones said, per Jon Machota of The Athletic.

Pickens is still only 25 years old, and if he can prove that last year's campaign was no fluke, Dallas would be wise to lock him up early in the offseason.

The Denver Broncos have three viable candidates for this list in receiver/returner Marvin Mims Jr., nickel back Ja'Quan McMilland, and cornerback Riley Moss. Heading into Week 1, though, Moss projects as the most valuable.

The 2023 third-round pick out of Iowa has developed into an above-average perimeter corner and a quality complement to star Patrick Surtain II. This past season, Moss started all 17 games, played 97 percent of the defensive snaps, and recorded 80 tackles to go with a league-high 19 passes defended (tied).

Moss allowed an opposing passer rating of 88.2 despite being regularly targeted as quarterbacks tried to avoid Surtain. The big question for Denver may be whether the team is willing to invest big money in both of its starting perimeter corners.

At only 26 years old, Moss should command a lucrative long-term deal on the open market.

The Detroit Lions have been quick to lock up offensive playmakers like Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and Jahmyr Gibbs. That trend should continue with tight end Sam LaPorta, likely before 2027 free agency.

The unknown is whether Detroit will view LaPorta as a bigger priority than standout safety Brian Branch. Both are scheduled to be free agents in the spring, and Detroit would prefer to keep them.

"We still want to keep those guys around. Those plans haven't changed," GM Brad Holmes said, per Colton Pouncy of The Athletic.

LaPorta is the healthier of the two right now, as Branch is on the PUP list following last year's Achilles tear. If he returns quickly and returns to form, though, Branch will probably be the more difficult player for the Lions to replace. LaPorta has been great when healthy, but those other aforementioned weapons give Detroit plenty of offensive flexibility.

Before suffering a torn ACL, tight end Tucker Kraft was establishing himself as the Green Bay Packers' go-to pass-catcher in 2025. He tallied 32 catches and 489 yards in his eight appearances, and he's on track to be an offensive focal point again in 2026.

It'll be a massive surprise if the Packers let the 25-year-old reach free agency. They might even have him signed before the start of the season.

"The Packers have a relatively strong offer out there to Tucker Kraft," ESPN's Adam Schefter said on The Pat McAfee Show .

The Packers clearly view Kraft as an important piece of the proverbial puzzle, and his contract should remain a priority until it's officially signed.

The Houston Texans might make a run at Super Bowl LXI due to the strength of their defense. Defensive tackle Tommy Togiai is a vastly underrated piece of that star-studded unit.

While Togiai doesn't have the name recognition of standouts like Danielle Hunter, Will Anderson Jr. or Derek Stingley Jr., he has become a very important rotational piece in Houston's defensive front. Last season, Togiai appeared in 15 games with six starts and played 51 percent of the defensive snaps. He recorded 59 tackles, 1.5 sacks, six tackles for loss, and four passes defended.

Set to turn 27 later this month, Togiai could be a quality contributor in Houston for years to come.

Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson turned 30 in March, but the eight-time Pro Bowler has shown no signs of approaching the proverbial cliff. He has started all 17 games in each of the past four seasons. In 2025, Pro Football Focus graded him 4th overall among all qualifying guards.

Nelson has been one of Indianapolis' most important players—and arguably its best overall—since he was taken sixth overall out of Notre Dame in 2018. He should be one of the Colts' top players again in 2026, and it would be a mild surprise if Indy even lets Nelson sniff the 2027 market.

The Colts are desperately hoping that Daniel Jones can rebound from last year's Achilles tear and prove that he's suited to be the franchise's long-term starting quarterback. Protecting Jones—and keeping Nelson—should be high on Indy's priority list.

Jacksonville Jaguars: WR Parker Washington

Re-signing Parker Washington could become less of a priority for the Jacksonville Jaguars if Travis Hunter really starts to develop as a receiver and/or if Brian Thomas Jr. finally returns to his standout rookie form. Right now, however, it's hard to see how the Jags could justify parting with Washington.

A 2023 sixth-round pick out of Penn State, Washington was a fine complementary receiver in his first two seasons before exploding in 2025. Last year, he appeared in 16 games, caught 58 passes, and led the team with 847 receiving yards.

If Washington remains one of Trevor Lawrence's favorite targets in 2026, retaining him for the long-term will be a must. Washington won't turn 25 until March.

We have to give an honorable mention to tight end Travis Kelce. The future Hall of Famer will turn 37 in October, but the Kansas City Chiefs are likely to welcome him onto the roster for as long as he wishes to play.

Kansas City won't be as committed to wide receiver Rashee Rice, who has much to prove in 2026. He missed most of the 2024 season with a torn LCL, and he missed six games last season due to suspension.

However, Rice has been the Chiefs' best wideout when he's been on the field. He's played just 28 career games in three seasons but has averaged 5.6 catches and 64.2 yards per game during that span.

If Rice can stay on the field and maintain that pace for a full 17-game campaign, Kansas City will be hard-pressed to let him reach the 2027 market.

This one could change, depending on the health of star Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers, who recently underwent a knee procedure . If Bowers battles injuries again this season, keeping fellow tight end and 2023 second-round pick Michael Mayer could become a top priority.

Assuming Bowers returns quickly and stays healthy, however, Las Vegas may look to lock up one of its other pass-catchers first.

Tre Tucker was the Raiders' top wideout in 2025. He started all 17 games and finished with five touchdowns and a team-high 696 receiving yards. While those aren't overly impressive numbers, it's worth recognizing that Las Vegas' passing attack was a borderline disaster last season.

Things should be better under new head coach Klint Kubiak, and Tucker should again be the Raiders' No. 1 receiver. If he maintains that role, keeping the 25-year-old will be a must. At some point, the Raiders will pivot to quarterback Fernando Mendoza , and he'll need all the quality receivers he can get.

Los Angeles Chargers: Edge Tuli Tuipulotu

The Los Angeles Chargers had one of the NFL's top defenses in 2025, and the emergence of Tuli Tuipulotu was a big reason why. The USC product had been productive in his first two seasons, but he truly broke through as an elite playmaker last year.

Tuipulotu recorded 49 tackles, 13 sacks, 20 tackles for loss, and 32 quarterback pressures en route to his first Pro Bowl nod.

As a 2023 second-round pick, Tuipulotu's rookie contract didn't include a fifth-year option. However, it would be a major shock to see Los Angeles let him walk away next offseason. Having just turned 24 earlier this month, Tuipulotu is just entering his playing prime and has all the hallmarks of a future franchise centerpiece.

The Los Angeles Rams have, arguably, the most loaded roster in the entire NFL. Unsurprisingly, they also have several important players scheduled to hit the 2027 free-agent market.

With all due respect to Kobie Turner, Byron Young, and Steve Avila, it's hard not to consider Puka Nacua priority No. 1. The BYU product tallied 4,191 yards and 19 touchdowns in his first three seasons, and he led the NFL in receptions last year. He also just turned 25 in May and should have a long and fruitful career ahead of him.

Receivers of Nacua's caliber aren't easy to find, and keeping one could be critical for Los Angeles' long-term outlook. At some point, they'll be forced to transition from Matthew Stafford to Ty Simpson at quarterback. Keeping Nacua should help ensure that the shift is a smooth one.

The Miami Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild and actively worked to turn over their roster during the offseason. They parted with the majority of their top players—though they did extend De'Von Achane—and they largely filled in their depth chart with unproven talent.

Following roster cuts, the Dolphins added a whopping seven players off of waivers.

While the process of turning over the roster may extend into the 2027 offseason, offensive tackle Austin Jackson is one key player who should be retained. The 2020 first-round pick was limited to 14 games over the past two seasons by toe and knee injuries but has been a solid starter when healthy.

Jackson has started 60 of the 62 games in which he has appeared and has settled in at right tackle. He'll need to prove he can stay healthy, of course, but he's still only 27 years old and can become a staple along the line.

We're projecting a bit here because we don't yet know how Kyler Murray will perform as the Minnesota Vikings' starting quarterback. However, he's Minnesota's top option right now, having unseated J.J. McCarthy early in training camp.

There are reasons to believe that Murray can recapture the Pro Bowl form he showcased early in his career, too. Kevin O'Connell is considered a QB-friendly head coach, and Minnesota boasts one of the top receiving corps in the league.

If Murray can take full advantage of pass-catchers like Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings, he should fully reestablish himself as an above-average NFL starter. If he does, the 29-year-old will likely become the most coveted quarterback in 2027 free agency.

The Vikings saw a similar situation unfold with Sam Darnold two years ago before allowing him to walk last offseason. If Murray thrives, Minnesota shouldn't make the same mistake twice.

The New England Patriots didn't win in their season opener, but their offensive line looked like a much better unit than it did in Super Bowl LX.

Mike Onwenu has been an integral part of New England's O-line pretty much since he entered the league as a 2020 sixth-round pick out of Michigan. He has appeared in 99 games with 91 starts and has started all 35 regular-season games since the start of the 2024 campaign.

Onwenu has settled in as the Patriots' right guard, but he has also spent time at left guard and offensive tackle over the years. He's a quality starter with a ton of positional flexibility, and he's still only 28 years old.

The rebuilding New Orleans Saints are clearly focused on their future. However, if edge-defender Cameron Jordan wants to return for his age-38 season, he'll probably be back in 2027.

As productive as Jordan still is—he had 10.5 sacks last season—re-signing defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd might be the bigger priority. He's several years younger than Jordan (33 in October), and he plays a position at which it's notoriously difficult to find high-end starters.

Shepherd only started eight games last season, but he appeared in 16 contests and played 67 percent of the defensive snaps. He recorded 47 tackles, three sacks, and 14 quarterback pressures while being credited with just two missed tackles.

New York Giants edge-defender Kayvon Thibodeaux recently took the top spot on B/R's trade block big board , and there's a reason for that. The Giants have two other standout edge-rushers in Brian Burns and Abdul Carter, and they may eventually put rookie linebacker Arvell Reese on the edge.

If New York does view Reese as a future sack artist, it may also view Thibodeaux as expendable. If that's the case, the Giants would be wise to trade him while they can.

Letting Thibodeaux walk for nothing in free agency would be foolish, and if the Giants plan to keep Reese at linebacker, re-signing Thibodeaux should be a priority. His production was down last season, but he recorded 11.5 sacks and 35 QB pressures in 2023.

Thibodeaux is a former top-five pick and is still only 25 years old. He's absolutely worth retaining as part of a deep edge rotation.

The New York Jets traded for quarterback Geno Smith early in the offseason, and they have high hopes for his ability to deliver some wins in 2026.

"I just feel like he's the guy that's going to lead us to the promised land," head coach Aaron Glenn said in March, per ESPN's Rich Cimini .

In all likelihood, Smith will lead the Jets to the 2027 draft, where they'll hold three first-round picks and will have the chance to chase their quarterback of the future. However, if the 35-year-old performs well during the regular season, retaining him and allowing him to play mentor to said quarterback-to-be-named would make a ton of sense.

Of course, this potential play could quickly unravel in 2026. There's no guarantee that Smith will play well after last year's disaster of a campaign with the Raiders. There's also no guarantee that he'll hold off rookie fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik , who could take over the bridge role if he performs admirably.

After extending both Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, the Philadelphia Eagles may not be able to afford keeping fellow defensive lineman Moro Ojomo. However, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio certainly hopes they can.

"I like him," Fangio said, per Johnny McGonigal of PennLive.com. "[GM] Howie [Roseman] needs to save some money for him, too."

Ideally, Roseman will find a way to keep Ojomo in the fold. While he isn't as recognized as Carter or Davis, the 2023 seventh-round pick has developed into a key cog in the defensive rotation. He appeared in all 34 games over the past two seasons, and he played 66 percent of the defensive snaps in 2025.

Last season, Ojomo also racked up 38 tackles, six sacks, and 21 quarterback pressures. Still only 25 years old, he'll draw a ton of interest if he reaches the open market.

The Pittsburgh Steelers may eventually reach a point where they're willing to move off of cornerback Joey Porter Jr. However, they would prefer to keep him and have made a contract offer ahead of Week 1—the Steelers traditionally have not negotiated after the start of the season.

The problem is that Porter is apparently dissatisfied with Pittsburgh's offer.

"It is not good enough for this one to be deemed close. But the Steelers are showing a willingness to engage," NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported on Tuesday (h/t Bleacher Report's Scott Polacek ).

While Pittsburgh may not be eager to match Porter's price tag on the open market, keeping him would be ideal. The 26-year-old has been an above-average starter for the Steelers since becoming a full-time starter midway through his rookie season.

Narrowing down the most important free agent for the San Francisco 49ers was admittedly tricky.

Mac Jones might be the best backup quarterback in the league. After last season's performance as a spot-starter, though, he's likely to receive starting opportunities—and starter money—in free agency. Jake Brendel, meanwhile, is a very good starting center, though he'll turn 35 near the start of next season.

With those factors considered, safety Ji'Ayir Brown appears to be the right choice here. He's been a regular starter since his 2024 sophomore season, he's allowed a career opposing passer rating of only 87.1 in coverage, and he won't turn 27 until January.

A few of San Francisco's top stars are likely nearing the end of their careers, but Brown should be a fixture of the future.

The defending champion Seattle Seahawks were willing to let a few key contributors—including Boye Mafe, Riq Woolen, and Kenneth Walker III—leave in free agency this offseason. They shouldn't face as many tough decisions in 2027, though they could have a tricky one with linebacker and edge-defender Uchenna Nwosu.

Nwosu will turn 30 in December and hasn't been a full-time starter since his first season with the Seahawks in 2022. However, the 2018 second-round pick was a valuable rotational player during last year's championship run.

Last season, Nwosu played 56 percent of the defensive snaps and recorded 35 tackles, seven sacks, three passes defended, and 23 quarterback pressures. He also recorded a pick-six in Super Bowl LX.

Though they did lose Mike Evans in free agency this year, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have typically done an excellent job of keeping their key players away from the open market.

Now that Mayfield is under contract on a new three-year extension, Tampa should turn its attention to linebacker and edge-defender YaYa Diaby. While the Louisville product has never produced elite sack numbers, he's a very impactful defender who has recorded 64 quarterback pressures over the past two seasons.

Diaby has also started all 34 regular-season games over the past two seasons while playing more than 70 percent of the defensive snaps. Still only 27 years old, he should be considered a building block of the Bucs' defensive future.

Tennessee Titans: Edge Jermaine Johnson II

We have to project a bit here because edge-defender Jermaine Johnson II Jermaine Johnson II has yet to take a regular-season snap with the Tennessee Titans.

A 2022 first-round pick of the Jets, Johnson was acquired in a trade in March. He was a logical addition for the Titans, as he previously played under head coach Robert Saleh when Saleh was in New York.

Johnson has also flashed high-end potential when healthy. A torn Achilles erased most of his 2024 campaign and may have impacted his 2025 performance. In 2023, however, he was a Pro Bowler who logged 7.5 sacks and 25 quarterback pressures.

Still only 27 years old, Johnson can become a defensive centerpiece in Tennessee if he can come close to replicating his 2023 form.

Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne entered the 2026 offseason as a logical trade candidate because of his hefty contract. Moving him now could still save Washington $17.4 million in cap space. With Payne on the roster entering Week 1, however, extending him might make a lot more sense.

Top-tier defensive tackles remain one of the rarest commodities in the modern NFL. While Payne isn't an elite interior defender, he's been an above-average starter throughout his eight-year career.

This past season, Payne tallied 46 tackles, three sacks, and seven tackles for loss in 15 starts. He's still only 29 years old and could be a defensive building block for the Commanders for several more seasons.

* Contract and cap information via Spotrac . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: 'We Need Each Other,' Chargers' Mike McDaniel Talks Jim Harbaugh Partnership Ahead of NFL Season
articles.summary: Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh are proof that finding someone whose unique personality matches your own that you should run with it.
articles.body:
Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh are proof that finding someone whose unique personality matches your own that you should run with it.

Leading up to their first game coaching together with the Los Angeles Chargers, McDaniel explained to ESPN's Kris Rhim "we need each other" when discussing his partnership with Harbaugh.

"We need each other," McDaniel said. "But that's kind of the beauty of the National Football League ... you learn quickly that every year you are putting your career in the hands of all of your teammates."

It's well known that Harbaugh has an interesting personality. As an example, he said earlier in the week that the start of the NFL season means he will "support no cause, foreign or domestic, other than the greatness of the Los Angeles Chargers."

McDaniel's quirkiness isn't as well-documented as Harbaugh's, but he can give you a unique soundbite from time to time.

Beyond some similar personality traits, though, another reason McDaniel and Harbaugh need each other is because of how complementary their coaching styles are.

Harbaugh's success as a head coach in college and the NFL has come from building rosters through the trenches with a strong running game.

McDaniel was praised at times during his tenure as head coach of the Miami Dolphins for his innovative offense, particularly the " cheat motion " before the snap that helped them rank near the top of the NFL in points scored.

After the Chargers finished just 20th in points scored last season, Harbaugh decided to make a change at offensive coordinator. Greg Roman, whose time with Harbaugh goes back to 2009 when they were together at Stanford, was fired two days after a 16-3 playoff loss to the New England Patriots.

McDaniel, who list his job with the Dolphins at the end of the season, was hired to replace Roman and add some new wrinkles to the offense with the goal of unlocking Justin Herbert's full skill set.

Time will tell if the marriage between Harbaugh and McDaniel pans out, but the prospect of this new offense with a quarterback like Herbert is extremely tantalizing.

McDaniel will get to show off what he has been cooking up for Herbert on Sunday when the Chargers host the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium in the season opener for both teams.

articles.summary: One day before kicking off the 2026 NFL season, the Detroit Lions restructured the contracts for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell to clear cap space.
articles.body:
One day before kicking off the 2026 NFL season, the Detroit Lions restructured the contracts for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell to clear cap space.

Per Spotrac's Michael Ginnitti, the restructures cleared $35.6 million against the cap for the Lions.

Detroit now has the second-most cap room available at just over $39 million. The San Francisco 49ers have the most cap space with roughly $49 million available.

Sewell is now set to count against the Lions' cap through the 2030 season with the final year being a void year worth $3.7 million .

He will only be 29 when his contract expires, so it's a safe bet he will get a new deal at some point as long as he stays healthy and continues to play at a high level.

St. Brown's deal has three void years that run through 2031. He can become a free agent after the 2028 season when he will also be 29 years old.

In addition to giving themselves some breathing room against the cap going into the start of the season, the Lions have also afforded themselves some flexibility if they want to make a significant in-season acquisition.

Detroit could also opt to roll over its unused cap space this season into 2027. The Lions currently have $97 million in cap room next year, but they currently only have 29 players under contract.

Sam LaPorta is the only key starter who is set to become a free agent after this season. Jared Goff could be in line for a new deal since his cap number jumps up to $62.6 million in 2027.

Whatever the plan ends up being, the Lions have set themselves up to be active during the season and next offseason if they choose to do so.

In the meantime, the Lions will kickoff their 2026 season on Sunday when they host the New Orleans Saints at Ford Field. Head coach Dan Campbell is 2-3 in season openers in his first five seasons with Detroit.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Lamar Jackson, Ravens' Relationship Amid Contract Extension Talks
articles.summary: Even though Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens did not work out a contract extension in the offseason, there doesn't appear to be any drama between the two sides like there was the last time they were negotiating a long-term deal.
articles.body:
Even though Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens did not work out a contract extension in the offseason, there doesn't appear to be any drama between the two sides like there was the last time they were negotiating a long-term deal.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the relationship between Jackson and the Ravens is the "healthiest it's been" with both parties having "every intention of continuing their work together for years to come."

Jackson is under contract through the 2027 season, so the Ravens have some wiggle room to get a new deal done.

Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta told reporters on Sept. 2 that he is "optimistic" they will work things out with Jackson before the start of free agency next offseason.

One reason for March to serve as an unofficial deadline is because Jackson is currently set to count $84.3 million against the 2027 cap.

Another reason for the Ravens to get a deal done sooner than later is Jackson is in a unique position of leverage over the organization. He negotiated a no-tag clause in the five-year, $260 million deal he signed in April 2023.

If Jackson plays out his current deal, the Ravens can't use the franchise tag to prevent him from becoming a free agent. He will be entering his age-31 season going in 2028, so a historic contract wouldn't be out of the question at that point.

It would also benefit the Ravens to get an extension done now rather than waiting because the top of the quarterback market is only going to go up. Patrick Mahomes and Dak Prescott are currently the only players making at least $60 million annually.

Of the 13 quarterbacks currently making at least $50 million per season, Jackson's contract is the only one set to expire before 2028.

The last time Jackson and the Ravens attempted to negotiate a long-term deal, things got contentious to the point that he publicly requested a trade because they "have not been interested in meeting my value" after they used the franchise tag on him.

Things eventually worked out between the two sides. Jackson won an MVP award in 2023 and finished second in 2024.

The Ravens have made the playoffs six times in eight seasons with Jackson as their starting quarterback.

articles.title: New Steelers Rumors on Joey Porter Jr. Contract Extension Talks, Potential Timeline for Deal
articles.summary: There is reportedly doubt regarding the Pittsburgh Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. agreeing to a contract extension before the team's 2026 regular-season opener on Sunday.
articles.body:
There is reportedly doubt regarding the Pittsburgh Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. agreeing to a contract extension before the team's 2026 regular-season opener on Sunday.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, the Steelers and Porter only began to engage in contract talks this week, and Jones has "not been overwhelmed with confidence" in the notion that they will strike a deal before Sunday afternoon.

Jones noted that the Steelers have a policy about not holding contract talks during the season, which means Porter could hit free agency next offseason if an agreement is not made before Sunday at 1 p.m. ET when Pittsburgh kicks off against the Atlanta Falcons.

Selected by Pittsburgh in the second round of the 2023 NFL draft out of Penn State, Porter has been a consistent starter over the course of his three-year NFL career.

Starting 41 of the 47 games he has appeared in, Porter has registered 165 tackles, three interceptions and 31 passes defended.

That includes 52 tackles, one pick and a career-high 14 pass breakups in 14 games last season.

Despite his solid play, Jones noted that there were "legitimate questions of whether the Steelers wanted to extend Porter" before they finally started holding talks with him this week.

The son of longtime Steelers linebacker Joey Porter, Porter Jr. is arguably Pittsburgh's top impending free agent along with linebacker Patrick Queen.

The Steelers are under new leadership this season with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin as head coach after Tomlin decided to end his 19-year tenure in Pittsburgh.

Tomlin led the Steelers to the playoffs in each of the past three seasons, however, Pittsburgh has not won a playoff game since 2016.

If the Steelers don't sign Porter to a new deal before Sunday afternoon, it is fair to wonder if the team's overall success or lack thereof in 2026 will weigh heavily on what they decide to do with Porter, Queen and other impending free agents.

Pittsburgh could always place the franchise tag on Porter or extend him after the season, but if the 26-year-old defensive back hits the open market, he figures to be one of top players available.

One day before their regular-season opener against the Minnesota Vikings, the Green Bay Packers reportedly agreed to a contract extension with tight end Tucker Kraft.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Packers and Kraft reached a four-year, $75 million deal that could be worth up to $92 million. The contract also includes a $26.5 million signing bonus.

A 2023 third-round draft pick out of South Dakota State, Kraft had been set to become a free agent at the end of the 2026 campaign.

After breaking out in 2024 with 50 receptions for 707 yards and seven touchdowns, Kraft was well on his way to a career year last season.

Through eight games, Kraft had registered 32 catches for 489 yards and six touchdowns, putting him on pace for likely Pro Bowl and All-Pro honors.

However, Kraft's season was cut short in Week 9 when he suffered a torn ACL against the Carolina Panthers.

Kraft spent the offseason working his way back from the injury, and he appears to be fully healthy, as he is not listed on the Packers' injury report ahead of their Week 1 game against the Vikings on Sunday.

Following the departure of wide receivers Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks during the offseason, Kraft figures to be among quarterback Jordan Love's top targets this season, along with the wideout trio of Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden.

Still just 25 years of age, Kraft's best years may very well be ahead of him, especially if he shows no ill effects from the torn ACL.
