articles.title: Bears Insider Rips 'Lazy' Narrative That Caleb Williams, Team Will Regress, 'We'll Use It For Fuel'
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears aren't entertaining any notion regarding potential regression following their successful 2025 season.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears aren't entertaining any notion regarding potential regression following their successful 2025 season.

One person with the Bears told The Athletic's Jonathan Jones the regression narrative is "lazy" and "we'll use it for fuel" as the team gets ready to start the 2026 season.

"I think it's lazy," the Bears source told Jones. "You see interceptions and say, 'You can't do that again.' Fourth-quarter comebacks and say, 'They can't come back.' And you're ignoring all the space in between that can be improved. We use it for fuel more than anything."

Regression is clearly something that has been a frequent topic of discussion in the Bears' building. Head coach Ben Johnson mentioned it early in training camp.

"Well, we're the No. 1 regression candidate so ... I think we've got plenty of motivation ourselves," Johnson said on July 31. "We talked about [quarterback] Caleb [Williams] in the past. He's used to handling a lot of attention, so I'm not worried about that."

It is hard not to look at the ways Chicago managed to get to 11 wins last season without thinking its not a sustainable model.

Seven of their 11 victories were in one-score games, with six coming when the Bears scored inside the final two minutes of regulation or in overtime. Their defense ranked 19th in EPA per play, a number that is propped up by forcing an NFL-high 23 interceptions. They also led the league with a plus-22 turnover differential.

That combination of turnover luck and late-game heroics are the perfect formula for negative year-over-year regression.

Per ESPN's Bill Barnwell , of the 21 teams excluding the 2025 Bears that have recorded a turnover margin of at least plus-20 since 1990, 20 of them won fewer games the year after and their average turnover margin was only plus-three.

There are ways for the Bears to negate the expected regression, though they didn't do much to improve their defense in the offseason. Coby Bryant, who was one of their big free-agent additions, will miss most of the season due to a knee injury that required surgery.

Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman, the No. 25 overall pick, is arguably the biggest addition to the defense.

On the offensive side of the ball, Caleb Williams taking another step forward would be huge. His down-to-down consistency, in particular, will be a point of emphasis. His 58.1 completion percentage in 2025 ranked 32nd out of 33 qualified quarterbacks.

Another hurdle facing the Bears is playing in arguably the deepest division in the NFL with the Green Bay Packers, Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings. All four teams in the NFC North finished over .500 last season.

The Bears will begin their quest to prove all the doubters and skeptics wrong on Sunday when they take on the Carolina Panthers in the season opener for both teams.

articles.title: Anthony Richardson's Agent Talks Colts QB's Trade Request, 'Abundantly Clear' Message From GM
articles.summary: Despite quarterback Anthony Richardson requesting a trade over the offseason, his agent does not expect one to materialize during the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Despite quarterback Anthony Richardson requesting a trade over the offseason, his agent does not expect one to materialize during the 2026 NFL season.

Speaking to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, agent Deiric Jackson said, "[Colts general manager] Chris [Ballard] has made it abundantly clear Anthony is gonna be here. I don't think I have to call him and say hey it's off the table. I think it's understood. And the Colts are going to do what's in the best interest of the Colts."

Before the 2025 season, the Colts signed Daniel Jones in free agency, and he was ultimately named the starter ahead of Richardson.

Jones' arrival and a fractured orbital bone suffered by Richardson meant the 2023 No. 4 overall pick did not see any game action last season.

In February, Jackson told ESPN's Stephen Holder that the Colts had granted Richardson permission to seek a trade. However, nothing came of it, and Richardson remained on the roster throughout training camp and the preseason.

Richardson is the Colts' QB2 behind Jones, meaning he will step in should anything happen to Jones, who is coming off a torn Achilles, which he suffered back in December.

The 24-year-old Richardson is entering a contract year in 2026, meaning he will be free to sign elsewhere in free agency next offseason.

It is unclear how much value he will have, though, after not playing last season and mostly struggling over his first two seasons.

In 17 career games, including 15 starts, Richardson has an 8-7 record, and he has completed just 50.6 percent of his passes for 2,400 yards, 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions, while also rushing for 634 yards and 10 scores.

Perhaps the Colts' stance on Richardson will change once the trade deadline approaches if Jones shows he is in solid form and fully recovered from the torn Achilles, but for now, it looks like Richardson will play out the remainder of his contract in Indy.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Talks 'Narrative' Around Himself, Drake Maye, Caleb Williams, 2024 NFL Draft QB Class
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Daniels made it clear he doesn't see his 2024 draft class peers' recent success as a motivator, noting that the "narrative" around the class, which includes Caleb Williams and Drake Maye, will shift year to year.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Daniels made it clear he doesn't see his 2024 draft class peers' recent success as a motivator, noting that the "narrative" around the class, which includes Caleb Williams and Drake Maye, will shift year to year.

"I'm happy for them," Daniels told ESPN's John Keim .. "We're all chasing a common goal and obviously you want to be the best, you want to win the Super Bowl, and I'm not rooting for them to do bad.

"There's a lot of stuff that's said of other people in my class and they should get that respect that they earned also. It was a different narrative our rookie year. So every year it's just going to be a flip-flop narrative and we're always going to get compared with each other, especially the top three picks."

Six quarterbacks were selected in the top 12 of the 2024 NFL draft , including the entire top three, which consisted of the Chicago Bears' Williams, Daniels and the New England Patriots' Maye.

Daniels got off to a hot start in 2024, earning Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year honors and leading the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game for the first time since 1991. Washington won 14 games (including playoffs), and Daniels accounted for 37 total touchdowns factor in the postseason.

He played just seven games during an injury-shortened 2025 season.

Meanwhile, a few QBs from that draft (Williams, Maye and the Denver Broncos' Bo Nix) just enjoyed great 2025 campaigns. Williams engineered some late-game magic en route to leading the Bears to an NFC North title.

Nix did the same as the Broncos earned the AFC's No. 1 seed and made the conference championship game. Maye, of course, guided the Patriots to an AFC title after a 14-win regular season, up 10 victories from the year prior.

As Daniels noted, people will always compare the 2024 draft class quarterbacks. However, another year brings new chances for the narratives to change.

Daniels, for his part, absolutely can return to his rookie year form. He helped turn around a long-struggling franchise in just one year thanks in part to his great play. He can lead another turnaround once again.

articles.title: Raiders' Kirk Cousins Talks Fernando Mendoza's Development, 'Just a Matter of Time'
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins will start the season as the Silver and Black's QB1, with 2026 No. 1 overall draft pick and reigning Heisman Trophy winner, Fernando Mendoza, waiting for his turn.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins will start the season as the Silver and Black's QB1, with 2026 No. 1 overall draft pick and reigning Heisman Trophy winner, Fernando Mendoza, waiting for his turn.

Cousins has great confidence Mendoza will figure it out soon enough, according to ESPN's Ryan McFadden .

"It's just a matter of time before it really gets to a point where he looks back and he says, 'Man, I really feel like I've got this,'" Cousins said.

McFadden also relayed some particulars on Cousins' thoughts regarding Mendoza.

"Cousins did say Mendoza has a great understanding of what it takes to be a pro, to learn a system and understand defenses," McFadden wrote. "Cousins said all those habits that Mendoza has displayed will lead to winning the long game and developing as a player."

Mendoza will learn behind Cousins for now as the veteran, on a one-year, $11.3 million deal , leads the Raiders into the start of head coach Klint Kubiak's era after the ex-Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator took over Las Vegas' sidelines.

The former Indiana star experienced an up-and-down preseason, completing 26-of-46 passes for 250 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. However, Mendoza has a bright future ahead if his collegiate career is any indication.

Mendoza showed great poise and leadership en route to leading Indiana to a 16-0 season and its first-ever national championship, which made him a surefire lock at No. 1 overall.

Cousins has faith in Mendoza's abilities moving forward. We'll see when Mendoza takes over down the line, but in the meantime, the Raiders will begin their season on Sunday at home against the Miami Dolphins.

articles.title: “I don't look at him any differently”: Patrick Mahomes' mother Randi Mahomes reflects on how his success in the NFL isn't the only thing she takes pride in
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback and Super Bowl champion, has always had a strong family support system even through the chall.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback and Super Bowl champion, has always had a strong family support system even through the challenging and difficult days he faced on the field. While Patrick Mahomes is easily one of the legendary athletes in the world, it is not the only thing his mother, Randi Mahomes, is proud of.Patrick Mahomes’ mother Randi Mahomes reflects on what really makes her proud of her Super Bowl champion sonA few years ago, in an interview with FOX4, Patrick Mahomes’ mother Randi Mahomes opened up about hes son as she said, "I am proud of the football, but the family part of it -- I'm way more proud and that`s something that I definitely don`t get enough of…”Patrick Mahomes’ mother Randi Mahomes added, "I don`t think it's really hit me because he's still my son," she said. "He is still Patrick, and my other two are still my kids. I don't look at him any differently today than I did five years ago."Randi Mahomes continued, "I am very, very proud…I always say we're blessed. He's blessed to be able to do his dream -- to live doing exactly what he loves."Patrick Mahomes’ mother Randi Mahomes has been a strong source of support and inspiration to the star playerAs Patrick Mahomes displayed immense talent since his childhood, many major leagues apart from the NFl expressed interest in onboarding him.Patrick Mahomes’ mother Randi Mahomes has often expressed how she was always worried that it might put a lot of pressure on him in his teenage years.A few weeks ago, Randi Mahomes made a heartfelt post about her son as he started the training camp as she wrote, “These years in the NFL have flown by, but watching you step into your purpose and chase your dreams has never stopped feeling special.🤍 Looking back through these photos just reminds me how far you’ve come and how much heart you’ve put into every single season.”She added, “I am so proud of the man you are, on and off the field. Here’s to your 10th year! To years of dedication, resilience, doing what you love, and to many more chapters ahead! I love you!”Interestingly, when Patrick Mahomes’ now wife Brittany Mahomes rejected his proposal when they were in school, it was his mother, Randi Mahomes, who he sought help from.Later, it was Randi Mahomes who gave him an idea of gifting her flowers on Valentine’s Day. As luck would have it, the plan worked out well and Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes began dating soon after.While Patrick Mahomes recently signed a $500 million extension with the Kansas City Chiefs and is one of the richest players in the league, he has not forgotten to take care of his family.A few months ago, the three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player gifted his mother, Randi Mahomes, a massive house, which she lives in now.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
